key_insight: Gliding-mammal-inspired wing and tail shapes create different aerodynamic trade-offs, with broader patagia maximizing lift and colugo-like tails improving pitch control while flat tails strengthen roll/yaw authority.
engineering_relevance: These morphology-dependent effects offer design guidance for bioinspired morphing aerial robots by linking membrane outline and tail geometry to lift, stability, and maneuverability targets.
method: Computational fluid dynamics used to isolate aerodynamic effects under controlled flow conditions
Compared three patagium configurations for lift, drag, stall, and pitching moment
Tested three tail/uropatagium configurations under baseline, symmetric-deflection, and asymmetric-deflection cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative CFD evaluation across multiple morphologies and deflection conditions, showing distinct performance and control responses rather than a single optimal shape.
watch_item: The findings come from controlled computational conditions, so real-world performance may differ when structural flexibility, unsteady flight, and fabrication constraints are included.
paper_title: Patagium and tail morphology shape aerodynamic performance and control authority in gliding-mammal-inspired wings
